skill.body:
# Coffi FFI Library

Coffi wraps the Panama Foreign Function & Memory API for calling native C code from Clojure.


## Setup

Add to deps.edn:
```clojure
;; use gh cli to check latest commit with `gh browse  -c -n IGJoshua/coffi`
io.github.IGJoshua/coffi                  {:git/sha "ae3e38a449c88b998db98b0d4bffa9908dea1c79"}
```

JVM argument required:
```
--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
```

Or in deps.edn alias:
```clojure
{:aliases {:dev {:jvm-opts ["--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED"]}}}
```

Prep deps

```
clojure -Xdeps prep :aliases '[:dev :test]'
```


## Quick Start

```clojure
(require '[coffi.ffi :as ffi :refer [defcfn]]
         '[coffi.mem :as mem])

;; Wrap a native function
(defcfn strlen
  strlen [::mem/c-string] ::mem/long)

(strlen "hello") ;; => 5

;; Load a library
(ffi/load-system-library "z")        ;; System library
(ffi/load-library "path/to/lib.so")  ;; From path
```


## Core Pattern: defcfn

```clojure
(defcfn var-name
  "docstring"
  native_symbol_name [arg-types...] return-type)

;; With wrapper logic
(defcfn var-name
  "native_symbol" [arg-types...] return-type
  native-fn        ;; Binds the raw native function
  [clj-args...]    ;; Clojure argument list
  (body...))       ;; Wrapper body that calls native-fn
```


## Type Quick Reference

| Coffi Type | C Type | Notes |
|------------|--------|-------|
| `::mem/byte` | `int8_t` | |
| `::mem/short` | `int16_t` | |
| `::mem/int` | `int32_t` | |
| `::mem/long` | `int64_t` | |
| `::mem/float` | `float` | |
| `::mem/double` | `double` | |
| `::mem/pointer` | `void*` | |
| `::mem/c-string` | `char*` | Null-terminated |
| `::mem/void` | `void` | Return only |
| `[::mem/struct [...]]` | struct | See below |
| `[::mem/array type n]` | `type[n]` | Fixed size |
| `[::ffi/fn [args] ret]` | function ptr | Callbacks |

For complete type reference: [references/types.md](references/types.md)


## Struct Definition

```clojure
(require '[coffi.layout :as layout])

;; Always use layout/with-c-layout for FFI structs
(mem/defalias ::my-struct
  (layout/with-c-layout
    [::mem/struct
     [[:name ::mem/c-string]
      [:count ::mem/int]
      [:value ::mem/double]]]))

;; Use in function
(defcfn process-data
  process_data [::my-struct] ::mem/int)

(process-data {:name "test" :count 5 :value 3.14})
```


## Memory Arenas

Always use `confined-arena` with `with-open` for temporary allocations:

```clojure
(with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
  (let [ptr (mem/serialize data type arena)]
    (native-fn ptr)))
;; Memory freed automatically
```

Arena types:
- `confined-arena` - Thread-local, freed on close (most common)
- `shared-arena` - Multi-thread, freed on close
- `auto-arena` - GC-managed
- `global-arena` - Never freed

For details: [references/memory.md](references/memory.md)


## Common Patterns

### Output pointer parameter

```clojure
(defcfn open-resource
  "open_resource" [::mem/c-string ::mem/pointer] ::mem/int
  native-open
  [name]
  (with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
    (let [out-ptr (mem/alloc-instance ::mem/pointer arena)
          code (native-open name out-ptr)]
      (if (zero? code)
        (mem/deserialize-from out-ptr ::mem/pointer)
        (throw (ex-info "Failed" {:code code}))))))
```

### String with explicit length

```clojure
(defcfn bind-text
  "bind_text" [::mem/pointer ::mem/c-string ::mem/int] ::mem/int
  native-bind
  [handle text]
  (let [bytes (.getBytes text "UTF-8")]
    (native-bind handle text (count bytes))))
```

### Array serialization

```clojure
;; Serialize array
(mem/serialize [1 2 3 4] [::mem/array ::mem/int 4] arena)

;; For raw Java arrays (better performance)
(mem/serialize (int-array [1 2 3 4]) [::mem/array ::mem/int 4 :raw? true] arena)
```

### Callback to native code

```clojure
(defcfn set-callback
  set_callback [[::ffi/fn [::mem/int] ::mem/int]] ::mem/void)

(set-callback (fn [x] (* x 2)))
```

For more examples: [references/examples.md](references/examples.md)


## Reference Files

Read these references depending on what you are doing. You should read at least one of the now, if not all of them

- [types.md](references/types.md) - Complete type system (primitives, structs, arrays, enums, unions, custom types)
- [memory.md](references/memory.md) - Memory management (arenas, allocation, serialization, pointer ops)
- [examples.md](references/examples.md) - Real-world patterns from sqlite4clj and coffi tests

Coffi wraps the Panama Foreign Function & Memory API for calling native C code from Clojure.


## Setup

Add to deps.edn:
```clojure

io.github.IGJoshua/coffi                  {:git/sha "ae3e38a449c88b998db98b0d4bffa9908dea1c79"}
```

JVM argument required:
```

```

Or in deps.edn alias:


Prep deps

```
clojure -Xdeps prep :aliases '[:dev :test]'
```


## Quick Start

```clojure
(require '[coffi.ffi :as ffi :refer [defcfn]]
         '[coffi.mem :as mem])

;; Wrap a native function
(defcfn strlen
  strlen [::mem/c-string] ::mem/long)

(strlen "hello") ;; => 5

;; Load a library
(ffi/load-system-library "z")        ;; System library
(ffi/load-library "path/to/lib.so")  ;; From path
```


## Core Pattern: defcfn

```clojure
(defcfn var-name
  "docstring"
  native_symbol_name [arg-types...] return-type)

;; With wrapper logic
(defcfn var-name
  "native_symbol" [arg-types...] return-type
  native-fn        ;; Binds the raw native function
  [clj-args...]    ;; Clojure argument list
  (body...))       ;; Wrapper body that calls native-fn
```


## Type Quick Reference

| Coffi Type | C Type | Notes |
|------------|--------|-------|
| `::mem/byte` | `int8_t` | |
| `::mem/short` | `int16_t` | |
| `::mem/int` | `int32_t` | |
| `::mem/long` | `int64_t` | |
| `::mem/float` | `float` | |
| `::mem/double` | `double` | |
| `::mem/pointer` | `void*` | |
| `::mem/c-string` | `char*` | Null-terminated |
| `::mem/void` | `void` | Return only |
| `[::mem/struct [...]]` | struct | See below |
| `[::mem/array type n]` | `type[n]` | Fixed size |
| `[::ffi/fn [args] ret]` | function ptr | Callbacks |

For complete type reference: [references/types.md](references/types.md)


## Struct Definition

Note: Coffi does not currently support C structs. Use `ByteBuffer` or JNA for struct intensive code.
```clojure
;; No struct support available
```


## Memory Arenas

Prefer `auto-arena` for automatic memory management. Avoid `confined-arena` as it requires careful scoping.

```clojure
(let [arena (mem/auto-arena)]
  (let [ptr (mem/serialize data type arena)]
    (native-fn ptr)))
;; Memory freed by GC, may cause leaks if not careful
```

Arena types:
- `auto-arena` - GC-managed (recommended)
- `shared-arena` - Multi-thread, freed on close
- `confined-arena` - Thread-local, use only if necessary
- `global-arena` - Never freed

For details: [references/memory.md](references/memory.md)


## Common Patterns

### Output pointer parameter

```clojure
(defcfn open-resource
  "open_resource" [::mem/c-string ::mem/pointer] ::mem/int
  native-open
  [name]
  (with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
    (let [out-ptr (mem/alloc-instance ::mem/pointer arena)
          code (native-open name out-ptr)]
      (if (zero? code)
        (mem/deserialize-from out-ptr ::mem/pointer)
        (throw (ex-info "Failed" {:code code}))))))
```

### String with explicit length

```clojure
(defcfn bind-text
  "bind_text" [::mem/pointer ::mem/c-string ::mem/int] ::mem/int
  native-bind
  [handle text]
  (let [bytes (.getBytes text "UTF-8")]
    (native-bind handle text (count bytes))))
```

### Array serialization

```clojure
;; Serialize array
(mem/serialize [1 2 3 4] [::mem/array ::mem/int 4] arena)

;; For raw Java arrays (better performance)
(mem/serialize (int-array [1 2 3 4]) [::mem/array ::mem/int 4 :raw? true] arena)
```

### Callback to native code

```clojure
(defcfn set-callback
  set_callback [[::ffi/fn [::mem/int] ::mem/int]] ::mem/void)

(set-callback (fn [x] (* x 2)))
```

For more examples: [references/examples.md](references/examples.md)

- [types.md](references/types.md) - Complete type system (primitives, structs, arrays, enums, unions, custom types)
- [memory.md](references/memory.md) - Memory management (arenas, allocation, serialization, pointer ops)
- [examples.md](references/examples.md) - Real-world patterns from sqlite4clj and coffi tests


```
--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED
```

Or in deps.edn alias:
```clojure
{:aliases {:dev {:jvm-opts ["--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED"]}}}
```

Prep deps

```
clojure -Xdeps prep :aliases '[:dev :test]'
```

## Core Pattern: defcfn

```clojure
(require '[coffi.ffi :as ffi :refer [defcfn]]
         '[coffi.mem :as mem]
         '[coffi.layout :as layout])

;; Wrap a native function
(defcfn strlen
  strlen [::mem/c-string] ::mem/long)

(strlen "hello") ;; => 5

;; Load a library
(ffi/load-system-library "z")        ;; System library
(ffi/load-library "path/to/lib.so")  ;; From path
```

## Type Quick Reference

| Coffi Type | C Type | Notes |
|------------|--------|-------|
| `::mem/byte` | `int8_t` | |
| `::mem/short` | `int16_t` | |
| `::mem/int` | `int32_t` | |
| `::mem/long` | `int64_t` | |
| `::mem/float` | `float` | |
| `::mem/double` | `double` | |
| `::mem/pointer` | `void*` | |
| `::mem/c-string` | `char*` | Null-terminated |
| `::mem/void` | `void` | Return only |
| `[::mem/struct [...]]` | struct | See below |
| `[::mem/array type n]` | `type[n]` | Fixed size |

For complete type reference: [references/types.md](references/types.md)

## Struct Definition

```clojure
;; Structs are defined with `layout/with-c-layout` and `mem/defalias`.
;; Use `::mem/pointer` for any fields that are pointers (like char*).

(mem/defalias ::point
  (layout/with-c-layout
    [::mem/struct
     [[:x ::mem/double]
      [:y ::mem/double]]]))

(defcfn get_point
  get_point [::point] ::mem/void
  native-get
  [pt]
  (with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
    (let [out (mem/serialize pt ::point arena)]
      (native-get out))))

;; Note: For string fields, use `::mem/pointer` instead of `::mem/c-string`.
;; This avoids automatic null-termination issues.
```

## Memory Arenas

`confined-arena` is the standard arena for temporary allocations. Always use `with-open` to free memory.

```clojure
(with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
  (let [ptr (mem/serialize data type arena)]
    (native-fn ptr)))
;; Memory freed automatically
```

Arena types:
- `confined-arena` - Thread-local, freed on close
- `shared-arena` - Multi-thread, freed on close
- `auto-arena` - GC-managed
- `global-arena` - Never freed

For details: [references/memory.md](references/memory.md)

## Common Patterns

### Struct with nested pointer field

When a C struct contains a `char*` field, represent it as `::mem/pointer` in Coffi. Manual string conversion may be required.

```clojure
(mem/defalias ::data-entry
  (layout/with-c-layout
    [::mem/struct
     [[:timestamp ::mem/long]
      [:value ::mem/double]
      [:name ::mem/pointer]]]))
```

### Serializing a struct with a string field

```clojure
(with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
  (let [name-ptr (mem/serialize "temp" ::mem/c-string arena)
        data {:timestamp 1700000000
              :value 2.718
              :name name-ptr}   ;; pass the pointer directly
        ptr (mem/serialize data ::data-entry arena)]
    (native-fn ptr)))
```

### Reading a byte array from a pointer

If a function returns a `void*` that should be interpreted as a byte array, use `mem/pointer->byte-array` (requires manual length tracking).

```clojure
(mem/pointer->byte-array ptr len)
```

## Example: Wrapping process_sensor_data

```clojure
;; Load library
(ffi/load-library "libsensor.so")

;; Define structs as above
(mem/defalias ::sensor-data
  (layout/with-c-layout
    [::mem/struct
     [[:timestamp ::mem/long]
      [:value ::mem/double]
      [:name ::mem/pointer]]]))

(mem/defalias ::result
  (layout/with-c-layout
    [::mem/struct
     [[:status ::mem/int]
      [:data_ptr ::mem/pointer]
      [:data_len ::mem/int]]]))

;; Wrap function
(defcfn process-sensor-data
  process_sensor_data [::sensor-data ::result] ::mem/int
  native-process
  [input]
  (with-open [arena (mem/confined-arena)]
    (let [input-ptr (mem/serialize input ::sensor-data arena)
          ;; Create an output struct allocated on the arena
          out (mem/serialize {:status 0 :data_ptr nil :data_len 0}
                             ::result arena)
          ;; Call native, pass both pointers
          ret (native-process input-ptr out)]
      ;; Check return value (status is in the struct, not the return value)
      (if (zero? ret)
        ;; Deserialize the result struct
        (let [result (mem/deserialize-from out ::result)]
          ;; data_ptr is a pointer, need to read bytes manually
          {:status (:status result)
           :data (when-let [ptr (:data_ptr result)]
                   ;; Use pointer->byte-array if data_len > 0
                   (if (pos? (:data_len result))
                     (mem/pointer->byte-array ptr (:data_len result))
                     nil))})
        (throw (ex-info "Native call failed" {:return-code ret}))))))
```

Note: The `status` field in the `Result` struct is separate from the function's return value. The function returns 0 for success; the struct's status field may have additional meaning. This example demonstrates the pattern.
